Ceramic electrolytes for lithium systems, from powder synthesis to printed tubes in molten metal.

I finished my PhD in August 2026 under Prof. Kyle Brinkman. The work covers Ga-doped LLZO garnet: how to make it at kilogram scale, how to shape it, and how it degrades in molten Li–Pb. I have five-plus years of R&D in ceramic processing, scale-up, characterization and electrochemical testing, four publications (two first-author) and one invention disclosure. I am looking for roles in solid-state batteries, advanced ceramics, and national lab research.

Case studies

SynthesisGarnet powder in 15 minutes, scaled to 1 kg per batch~90% yield · 94.2% dense · 5.8 × 10⁻⁴ S cm⁻¹ at 30 °C
Problem
The usual solid-state route to LLZO needs long milling, 900–1100 °C calcination and excess lithium. Wet-chemical routes use toxic reagents and extra steps. The goal was cubic Ga-LLZO powder that is fast to make, scales, and sinters to high density.
Variables
Fuel-to-oxidizer ratio (0.5 to 1.5), calcination temperature (750 to 950 °C), lithium excess (10%), Ga content (0.5 per formula unit) and sintering temperature (1000 to 1200 °C).
Decisions
A ratio of 0.5 gave the highest yield (90%), the smallest crystallites (62 nm) and phase-pure cubic powder. Fuel-rich ratios left Li₂CO₃ and La₂Zr₂O₇ behind, and yield fell to 71% at 1.5, likely from powder displaced by gas evolution. Powder calcined at 750 °C was the finest, which suits sintering. Sintering at 1100 °C reached 94.2% density. 1150 and 1200 °C added density but gave rougher surfaces and abnormal grain growth.
Validation
XRD with Rietveld refinement, TGA/DSC and FTIR traced the reaction path: urea–nitrate complex, amorphous phase, La₂Zr₂O₇, then cubic Ga-LLZO near 750 °C. FE-SEM, EDS, HAADF-STEM and HRTEM checked structure and elemental uniformity. EIS on Li|LLZO|Li cells gave conductivity and activation energy.
Outcome
Cubic Ga-LLZO in 15 minutes at ~90% yield. Batches scaled from 5 g to 1 kg, about 200×. Sintered pellets reached 94.2% relative density and 5.8 × 10⁻⁴ S cm⁻¹ at 30 °C, with an activation energy of 0.3 eV.
Fabrication3D-printed LLZO tubes for tritium extraction25 tubes delivered to SRNL · no cracking or leakage
Problem
Tritium can be pulled out of molten Li–Pb by direct electrolysis through a Li-conducting ceramic. That needs LLZO in a form that scales, and closed-end tubes are the target geometry. A tube has to survive printing, debinding and sintering without cracking, then hold a seal.
Variables
Slurry solids loading, binder and dispersant, print geometry and extrusion rate, laser power for drying each layer, debinding and sintering schedule, lithium excess, and the mother-powder bed.
Decisions
Direct ink writing with a CO₂ laser drying each layer at 7.5 W. An aqueous slurry at 50 wt.% solids with HPMC binder. Reactive sintering at 1150 °C for 10 h, which forms the cubic phase and densifies in one step. A 20% lithium excess in the powder and a sacrificial mother-powder bed to offset lithium loss.
Validation
Archimedes density, XRD and Rietveld phase fractions, SEM microstructure, gas flow-meter and gas chromatography leak checks, Li-pumping voltage sweeps at 350 °C, and immersion tests in molten Li–Pb.
Outcome
25 tubes delivered to SRNL with no cracking or leakage. Relative density about 92%. The tubes in the 2024 Materials Letters paper were 88% dense and over 90% cubic. Li was pumped through the tubes at 350 °C. An invention disclosure on the fabrication method is filed with the Clemson University Research Foundation.

Fabrication route

  1. MillLi₂CO₃ (20% excess), La₂O₃, ZrO₂ and Ga₂O₃ ball-milled together.
  2. Slurry50 wt.% solids in water with HPMC binder and a dispersant.
  3. PrintLayer-by-layer extrusion into a closed-end tube. A CO₂ laser at 7.5 W dries each layer before the next.
  4. SinterReactive sintering at 1150 °C for 10 h under sacrificial mother powder. Phase formation and densification happen in one step.
Failure analysisWhy Ga-LLZO degrades in molten Li–Pb and Ta-LLZO does notGa: cubic to tetragonal, Pb at grain boundaries · Ta: ~2 µm surface layer
Problem
LLZO is a candidate membrane for extracting tritium from molten Li–Pb in fusion blankets. It has to keep its conductive cubic phase in a hot, lithium-rich, reducing melt. Which dopant survives, and up to what temperature?
Variables
Dopant (Ga or Ta at the same nominal 0.5 per formula unit, same synthesis route), temperature (350 and 450 °C), exposure time (up to 100 h), and geometry (pellets and tubes).
Decisions
Compared pellets to isolate the dopant effect and used tubes as a second check. Built a sealed ConFlat cell with a movable sample holder, argon flow and a Ta-lined alumina crucible, and withdrew samples slowly to limit residual Li–Pb on the surface. Heated exposed samples in air to test whether the damage is reversible.
Validation
XRD and Rietveld refinement for phase fractions, FE-SEM and EDS cross-sections for Pb penetration, EPR for reduction-induced defects, XPS depth profiles, ICP-MS for composition, TGA/DSC, and oxide-melt solution calorimetry for formation enthalpy.
Outcome
At 350 °C, Ga-LLZO tubes held their cubic phase for 100 h. At 450 °C, Ga-LLZO transformed from cubic to tetragonal (70% of the pellet in 50 h), cracked, and took in Pb along grain boundaries. Ta-LLZO stayed cubic with a ~2 µm reaction layer. Its formation enthalpy from the oxides is more negative: −843 ± 8 kJ/mol against −381 ± 4 kJ/mol for Ga-LLZO. Reheating in air partly reversed the damage in Ga-LLZO, so the mechanism is reduction-driven.

Other engineering work

Hardware

Custom high-temperature test systems

Built a multi-sample impedance system (room temperature to 500 °C) and a sealed inert-atmosphere cell for molten Li–Pb exposures at 350–450 °C, up to 100 h. Tested Li|LLZO|Li symmetric cells by EIS, cyclic voltammetry, critical current density and 100 h Li stripping/plating.

Reliability

Glass seals for SOFCs

Screened three sealants for 350–650 °C service with thermal cycling, helium leak testing, DSC, CTE mismatch and adhesion tests. Schott GM31107 was selected.

Schematics and interactive figures

Solvent-free combustion synthesisSchematic

  • Mix

    Metal nitrates and urea ground together in a mortar until a gel forms. Li at 10% excess.

  • Combust

    Gel in an alumina crucible goes into a preheated furnace for 15 minutes.

  • Collect

    White, fluffy cubic Ga-LLZO powder at ~90% yield. Fuel-to-oxidizer ratio 0.5.
